steps.message:
# Some coins misbehave in the flooded cave

### What happens
`recording.mp4` is an uncut run through a flooded cave basin. Partway through the clip, Tux does something that releases a group of new coins. From that moment until the end of the clip, those coins do not behave the way coins in this game should. The coins that were already placed in the level, Tux, the fish and the scenery in the recording are correct.

### Expected
The released coins should behave like a normal coin burst in this game, from the moment they spread out of the block until they come to rest and Tux collects them on contact. Once a coin is in the water it should drift down slowly. Fix every way the released coins behave wrongly in the recording.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4` (44 seconds)

You can inspect individual moments of the video by extracting frames from it with `ffmpeg`.

Inspect the attached file before making changes.

steps.message:
I've made the fixes, but they aren't confirmed yet: the build to check that they compile is still running in the background, and I haven't played the level again to compare with the recording.

**What the recording shows:** when Tux hits the block, the released coins all fly to the right and partly downward. They drop to the floor quickly even though they're underwater, keep hopping and sliding around, and stay there while Tux swims through them.

**The causes and fixes:**
1. **One-sided spread** (`src/object/coin_explode.cpp`): the left/right sign was applied to the vertical speed instead of the horizontal one. So every coin went right, and half of them were thrown downward. It now applies to the horizontal speed, so the coins fan out upward on both sides of the block.
2. **Tux couldn't collect them** (`src/object/coin.cpp`): the released coins were in a collision group that only hits the level geometry, so they never touched Tux. They're now in `COLGROUP_MOVING`. Rock, Trampoline and Crusher already have special cases for these coins, which only make sense with that group.
3. **They never came to rest:** a coin bounced again whenever it landed faster than 20, and a bounce sends it back up at 99. So it never got below that limit and kept bouncing and sliding forever. Now it only bounces when landing faster than 200; otherwise it stops completely, sideways speed included.
4. **No water handling:** the released coins now check whether they're in water. If so, gravity drops to 20% (the same value Rock uses) and falling speed is capped at 80, so they drift down slowly. The 80 cap is my own choice, so check that it feels right when you play.

Coins that were already placed in the level use a different path and aren't affected.
